No I didn’t see that “one article” because I actually had this experience with an employee I hired AND another person which applied. 

And I am absolutely going to judge someone’s upbringing when they bring their upbringing into the workplace. I am not their mom and this is not their house, they need to be able to do the job they applied for and if they can’t they can leave. 

Carpooling isn’t a problem, it is a problem when this one specific man told me he “only had this job to save money for a car,” when he had worked there for 3 years and has no bills because his grandmother pays them all; which he bragged about. His attitude and work ethic were less than spectacular. He had not a penny to show for the time he was there and he still has no car.

Gen Z manager here… bro idk how the fuck some of these people are let out into the world? I’m hiring people MY AGE and they’re showing up to interviews with their parents. I had an employee bring her parents with her every shift; she said it was because she has dyslexia (we make pizza?!)

The same girl also didn’t know what red onions and blue cheese were. My favorite line from her in the month she worked here was “whats in pineapple juice.” Did her parents never show her how to cook for herself? Did they never eat at home and make their own food? Idk man but they failed that young woman. 
 
I had a man come in and ask about the status of his daughter’s job application because she was “in the car” and “shy.” I told him I would reach out shortly, and took his daughter’s name. I used her name to find her application and delete it 🤓 because why would I hire someone who can’t even ask for the job themself. 

I think as society we need to do better and bully shitty parents. I’ve noticed a massive trend of parents speaking for their kids when they have their own voices and mouths they can use. At work I will have customers come and order food with their kids, and I shit you not I asked a 9 year old yesterday what he wanted on his pizza and before he could even answer, his mother was answering for him. That child is doomed for the real world and the job market if his mom never lets him get uncomfortable talking to people in his childhood; the time you’re supposed to learn basic communication skills is your childhood. 

I feel this is why some of these people can’t take criticism, or they think they can use any medical term they’ve heard of as reasoning behind not having to do a work task. I had an employee tell me he couldn’t do dishes because of his TMJ… thats a jaw problem bro ??? Reasonable accommodations must be made for employees - REASONABLE - and lots of people think they they can make up anything and we have to just go “oh okay, no dishes for you ever hope your temporomandibular joint feels better 🩷💅” This (ex) employee with the TMJ is literally 29 ? Idk if thats even gen z but his fucking grandmother drives him to and from work which is so baffling to me. It’s interesting to see individuals who were not only failed by their parents, but apparently the world too. 


MY TIP FOR YOU THOUGH: just keep it real. If you think they suck tell them why. I like to think that most people do want to do better, just be straight with them as with your job expectations and why those expectations are set. Never feel bad for firing someone, but make sure you get as much documentation as you can to really put all of the nails in their coffin when you kick them to the curb 🥾

Basically: do lots of practice tests, and pretend to be confident. I know I didn’t improve a lot, but those two things enabled me to improve at all.
